How matching works.
  • Style ranks the VFL player against VFL players at his position and the AFL player against AFL players at his. Two players with the same shape match even if one plays at a lower level.
  • Level first converts the VFL line to a projected AFL line (using how much each stat shrank for players who went from VFL to AFL the next season), then ranks it against real AFL players at the position. A high match here means he projects to produce like that player.
  • Disposal efficiency is on the radar when the AFL season is 2026, the only AFL season with it so far. For players who played both levels in 2026 it barely moved (72.4% in the VFL, 72.2% in the AFL), so Level mode carries it across unchanged.
  • Match score is 100 minus the average gap in percentile points across the 12 radar stats, so 90 means the two profiles sit about 10 percentile points apart on average.
  • VFL positions come from the player's AFL position where he has one, otherwise from the AFL players his stats sit closest to. That method picks the right AFL position about two times in three, so check the position tag.
  • Pressure acts, metres gained, spoils and other Champion Data stats aren't recorded for the VFL, so they're left out. Small VFL samples are pulled toward the position average. AFL players need 5+ games.
